title: Get started
text: popAddTrend() adds poll aggregation. default Kalman filter, treats true support party random walk every poll noisy measurement , weighted sample size. sd daily standard deviation random walk: larger values follow polls closely. filter looks back time. smoothing = TRUE, every estimate also takes later polls account, removes lag behind sudden changes. estimates calculated dates polls; linearInterpolation turns daily series. smoothed trend method behind POLITICO’s kalmanSmooth trend: plot() draws polls points every trend line. Trends variance, Kalman trends, come 95 % uncertainty band. plot chunk unnamed-chunk-7
code: at = popAddTrend(at, name = 'filtered', type = 'kalman', args = list(sd = 0.003)) at = popAddTrend(at, name = 'smoothed', type = 'kalman',                  args = list(sd = 0.003, smoothing = TRUE),                  interpolations = list(linearInterpolation = list())) names(at$trends) #> [1] "kalmanSmooth" "kalman"       "filtered"     "smoothed" both = merge(at$trends$smoothed, at$trends$kalmanSmooth, by = c('date', 'party')) both[, .(days = uniqueN(date), meanAbsDifference = mean(abs(value.x - value.y)))] #>     days meanAbsDifference #>    <int>             <num> #> 1:  4735      0.0005051443 at$trends$kalmanSmooth = NULL at$trends$kalman = NULL plot(at, xlim = c('2024-01-01', NA))

title: Get started
text: popAddTrend() also takes function. gets popPolls object data returns long table columns date, party value (optionally variance). example, median polls last weeks: plot chunk unnamed-chunk-14
code: rollingMedian = function(data, days = 21) {     polls = popLong(data)[date >= as.Date('2024-01-01')]     dates = seq(min(polls$date), max(polls$date), by = 'week')     polls[, .(date = dates,               value = vapply(dates, function(d) median(value[date > d - days & date <= d]),                              numeric(1))),           by = party] }  at = popAddTrend(at, type = rollingMedian, args = list(days = 28)) plot(at, xlim = c('2024-01-01', NA))

title: Load and Analyse European Poll of Polls Data
text: popRead() returns popPolls object, list data.tables: Shares stored fractions (0.27 = 27 %); seat projections NL-parliament stored absolute numbers. popLong() returns polls, elections trends long format.
code: library(pollofpolls)  # Overview of all available polls (visits every country page once, cached afterwards) popGetInfo()  # Read German national parliament polls de = popRead('DE-parliament') de  # Plot the polls plot(de) plot(de, xlim = c('2025-01-01', NA))  # Add trends de = popAddTrend(de, name = 'Kalman', type = 'kalman', args = list(sd = 0.003)) de = popAddTrend(de, name = 'Rolling mean 30d', type = 'weightedMeanLastDays',                  args = list(days = 30)) plot(de)  # Get a description of the available trends and interpolations ?popAddTrend

title: Load and Analyse European Poll of Polls Data
text: Trends can post-processed lastInterpolation, linearInterpolation bernoulliConvInterpolation. Kalman trends come variance, plot() shows uncertainty band (bands = FALSE switch ). smoothing = TRUE every estimate Kalman filter also takes later polls account. Interpolated daily values, reproduces kalmanSmooth trend POLITICO publishes: type also takes function, gets popPolls object data returns data.frame columns date, party value (optionally variance):
code: de = popAddTrend(de, name = 'Kalman smoothed', type = 'kalman',                  args = list(smoothing = TRUE),                  interpolations = list(linearInterpolation = list())) lastPoll = function(data) popLong(data)[, .(value = data.table::last(value)), by = .(date, party)] de = popAddTrend(de, type = lastPoll)

title: Load and Analyse European Poll of Polls Data
code: # Support, uncertainty and change over the last 30 days according to the trend added last popLatest(de)  # Seat projection (national level only, no direct mandates or overhang seats) popSeats(de, seats = 630, threshold = 0.05, method = 'sainte-lague')  # Polling firms and their deviation from the consensus, by party popFirms(de) popHouseEffects(de)

title: Add Trend to Polls — popAddTrend
text: Available trend functions : kalman Kalman filter, arguments: sd = 0.003, daily standard deviation true support share scale, smoothing = FALSE. smoothing = TRUE every estimate takes later polls account well (Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoother). estimates calculated dates polls ; together linearInterpolation smoothed trend reproduces POLITICO's daily kalmanSmooth trend. kalmanKFAS Kalman filter based KFAS package, arguments: sd = 0.003, smoothing = TRUE. weightedMeanLastDays Linearly weighted rolling mean, arguments: days = 30, maxObs = Inf. ident Plain mean polls published day, arguments. Instead name, type can function. called popPolls object argument data elements args, return data.frame columns date, party (codes data$parties) value, plus optionally variance, used uncertainty bands. Available interpolations : lastInterpolation Carries last value forward, arguments. linearInterpolation Linear interpolation, arguments. bernoulliConvInterpolation Binomial smoothing consecutive trend values, arguments: n = 20, k = 6. Interpolations keep variance trend, interpolated (smoothed) like values; two dates polls therefore approximation.

title: Add Trend to Polls — popAddTrend
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ de = popRead('DE-parliament') de = popAddTrend(de, name = 'Kalman 0.003', type = 'kalman', args = list(sd = 0.003)) de = popAddTrend(de, name = 'Kalman smoothed', type = 'kalman',                  args = list(smoothing = TRUE),                  interpolations = list('linearInterpolation' = list())) plot(de)  # a custom trend: the median of the polls of the last 14 days rollingMedian = function(data, days = 14) {     polls = popLong(data)     dates = seq(min(polls$date), max(polls$date), by = 'day')     polls[, .(date = dates,               value = vapply(dates, function(d) median(value[date > d - days & date <= d]),                              numeric(1))), by = party] } de = popAddTrend(de, type = rollingMedian, args = list(days = 21)) } # }
